nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Periodic sweep (research.md §4) — every run both cancels any follow-up whose lead has since closed/opted-out/replied (FR-027) and, for anything past the configured delay, creates the next reviewable draft (FR-026/FR-028). All of that logic lives behind /followups/due, not in this workflow.

nodes.name: Call /followups/due
nodes.notes: GET only — eligibility (consent, opt-out/reply/spam, delay elapsed, attempt cap) is decided entirely by packages/business-rules/src/follow-up.ts behind this route, not by this node.

nodes.name: Split Out Due Follow-ups
nodes.notes: The route returns zero or more eligible follow-ups in `body` (an array) — split so the per-item logging below runs once per newly-due follow-up, not once for the whole batch.

nodes.name: Call /events (log follow-up created)
nodes.notes: A reviewable follow-up draft requires its own approval (FR-029, default policy) — this workflow only ever creates the draft and logs it; it never calls /drafts/{id}/approve or /email/send itself. The dashboard's existing Approval Queue (already generic over any pending_approval ReplyDraft) is where a human approves it, which reuses WF-02 unchanged.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ leadId: $json.leadId, workflowName: 'wf-03-follow-up-scheduler', eventType: 'follow_up', status: 'success', safeMetadata: { followUpId: $json.followUpId, attemptNumber: $json.attemptNumber, draftId: $json.draftId, outcome: 'awaiting_approval' } }) }}
